tonight.headline: Your three claims landed two of three. There is nothing left to do in Chem today, and that is the whole report.
body: Week 2 has not kicked off — the first ball is Josh Allen's, Thursday 18:15 in Mexico City. ESPN has you 126.2 to Panda Attack's 124.8 and prices it at 51%. Your lineup already matches every position this brief holds, so no starter changes.

The waiver run at 07:14 gave you Jalen Coker and Tyler Loop and cost you Tampa Bay: Footballers claimed the Buccaneers defense ahead of you and you took the Ravens fallback. The consequence is that three roster seats changed hands ninety minutes ago, which closes them, and there is nothing on this roster that can honestly be dropped today. The Do-first list is empty and that is the correct answer, not a thin one.

case.label: What decides the week
case.body: Panda Attack start Dak Prescott, Chase Brown, Saquon Barkley, Javonte Williams in the flex, George Pickens and Davante Adams. Three of their nine starters are Dallas players facing Washington, so their week is highly correlated: one Cowboys blowout moves their whole total at once, in either direction. Yours is spread across six games and two of them are Thursday and Monday.

case.label: Where you are actually ahead
case.body: Josh Allen against the Lions' defense, ranked 29th of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 board, is the single biggest projected edge on either roster. Panda Attack's counter is Jalen Hurts — on their bench, where he scores them nothing, because they can only start one quarterback.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Panda Attack swap Javonte Williams out of the flex, or Dallas and Washington produce the shootout their 27th-ranked defences point at, in which case the correlation runs their way rather than against them. Either way the 51% is ESPN's number on a 1.4-point projected gap in Week 2, which is noise, and nothing in this brief acts on it.

whatWentWrong.title: You lost Tampa Bay. Footballers claimed the Buccaneers defense at 07:14 and you took the Ravens fallback.
whatWentWrong.lead: The reasoning held — Tampa Bay is 1st of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 board. The queue position did not. Footballers sat 9th in priority, you sat 10th, and one place decided it.

case.label: What actually happened
case.body: At 07:14 Footballers added the Buccaneers D/ST and dropped New England. Your queue then fell through to Baltimore, which you now own. Baltimore is 3rd of 32 on the same board against New Orleans, who are 26th as an offense — so the fallback is a good defense with a good draw, not a consolation.

case.label: Why it still cost something
case.body: It cost you the seat, not the points. The defense slot has now moved three times in eight days — Jacksonville in, Jacksonville out, Baltimore in — and the seat is closed for seven days from this morning. That is why San Francisco, 4th of 32 this week with the largest ownership move on the entire wire at +23.95, is a watch row below instead of a card.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2 while San Francisco finishes top 5 — then the churn rule cost you real points and the next brief says so rather than defending the hold.

whatWentWrong.title: Nothing on this roster is droppable today, and that is the direct cost of firing three claims at once.
whatWentWrong.lead: Coker, Loop and the Ravens all arrived at 07:14. Likely arrived 13 September, Brian Thomas Jr. 12 September. Every remaining bench seat carries a written hold.

case.label: The arithmetic
case.body: Fourteen rostered players. Nine are starters you are not benching. Three arrived ninety minutes ago. Brian Thomas Jr. is four days old with an intact thesis. That leaves Kyle Pitts, held in writing this morning, and Kyle Monangai, whose drop is already on the record as a mistake — he was cut for Tre Tucker on 13 September and scored 20.4.

case.label: What it is costing you
case.body: Real names. Romeo Doubs is a free agent here at 59.7% rostered and is FantasyPros' priority Week 2 pickup because A.J. Brown went to injured reserve. Khalil Shakir, Xavier Worthy and Jakobi Meyers are all free and all above 68% rostered. In a ten-team league that is a blundered wire, and you cannot reach it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Brian Thomas Jr. being ruled out at Denver on Friday's report. That is the one condition on the record that reopens a seat, and the claim that fills it should be Doubs, not a re-add of Stefon Diggs.

worthALook.name: 49ers D/ST
worthALook.lead: 4th of 32 this week, the largest ownership move anywhere on this wire, a free agent — and you should not touch him.

case.label: Why the market moved
case.body: San Francisco's roster share rose 23.95 points in one day, more than three times the next-biggest move on the Chem wire. The reason is the opponent: Miami start Malik Willis, six career starts and 155 career attempts, and FantasyPros' Week 2 column says his debut 'did not inspire confidence'. That is a matchup the whole market can see at once.

case.label: Why you hold Baltimore anyway
case.body: Baltimore is 3rd of 32 on the same board and San Francisco 4th. ESPN's weekly numbers are 7.6 against 7.8. You are being offered two tenths of a point to move a seat that changed hands ninety minutes ago and three times in eight days — and the log has two CHURN entries about exactly this slot.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Baltimore finishes outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2, the seat is open again on Tuesday and San Francisco is the first name on the list. Not before. A stream that gains 0.2 costs a roster move for nothing.

worthALook.name: Romeo Doubs
worthALook.lead: FantasyPros' priority Week 2 pickup, free here, and the only reason he is a watch row is that you have nothing to drop.

case.label: The vacated role
case.body: A.J. Brown is on injured reserve — he sits on Nicky Jam's roster in this league at 0.0 projected — and FantasyPros name Doubs the priority pickup replacing him. This is the add shape the strategy file ranks second behind raw opportunity: someone got hurt and this player inherits the work, and he already plays the snaps.

case.label: The blocked seat, and why
case.body: Two different blocks, not one. Coker, Loop and the Ravens arrived at 07:14 today; Likely 2.5 days ago; Brian Thomas Jr. 3.6 days ago — all inside the seven-day churn window. The three older seats are blocked for a different reason: Pitts carries a hold written this morning, Monangai's drop is already logged as a mistake, and Tuten at 205.2 season out-projects Doubs at 150.1, so cutting him would lower projected points, which the strategy file treats as a hard floor.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Brian Thomas Jr. is ruled out at Denver on Friday's report, that seat reopens by its own stated condition — and Doubs is the claim, not a re-add of Stefon Diggs. Chem priority resets weekly so it costs nothing lasting. Also act if Doubs clears 8 targets in Week 2 while still unrostered here.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: 76% rostered nationally and dropped by JuiceJam this morning. It looks like the ownership anomaly you want. It is not.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: T.J. Hockenson, a tight end, was Minnesota's second target option behind Justin Jefferson in Week 1 — 81% route share, 16% target share. Addison is therefore third at best in an offence whose quarterback is in concussion protocol. A 76% ownership figure is a memory of what he was, and the -2.71 daily move says the market is correcting it now.

case.label: Who dropped him and why it matters
case.body: JuiceJam cut him at 07:14 to claim Devaughn Vele. That is a manager with the same information choosing a 35%-owned New Orleans receiver over him. Once is an error; the national picture agrees — RotoBaller published a column on 15 September titled 'Should I Drop Jordan Addison for Week 2?'

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kyler Murray clearing the five-stage protocol and Addison drawing 7+ targets in Week 2, or Jefferson missing time. Either makes him the second read rather than the third. I could not retrieve the body of the RotoBaller piece, only its headline, and I am not treating a headline as a finding beyond what it plainly says.

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: The highest-rostered kicker on this wire at 85%, and he is eight places worse than the one you claimed this morning.

case.label: The comparison you asked for
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 kicker board has Tyler Loop K4 and Eddy Pineiro K12. The best kicker actually available to you here is Chase McLaughlin at K6, 16.4% owned; Tyler Bass is K8 at 5.9%; Cairo Santos K14; Chris Boswell, whom you just dropped, K17. Loop beats every one of them.

case.label: Why ownership is the wrong signal
case.body: Pineiro's 85% is a draft-day artifact — he was taken as a top-five kicker and nobody has cut him. Loop is at 52.7% because he was a rookie question mark until Week 1. Baltimore host New Orleans, who are 26th of 32 as an offence, which is the best scoring environment any kicker on this wire has.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop finishing outside the top 20 kickers in Week 2 while Baltimore's implied team total falls below 22 for two straight weeks. That is the falsification clause already on the record for the Loop claim and it is unchanged.

settled.title: Claim Jalen Coker, drop Matthew Stafford (16 September)
settled.result: Landed at 07:14. Coker is yours. He is QUESTIONABLE with the ankle, calls it a rolled ankle from the first quarter against Chicago and expects to play at Atlanta. Draft Sharks have him at 16.0 PPR per game over his last eight.

settled.title: Claim the Buccaneers defense, drop the Jaguars defense (16 September)
settled.result: Lost. Footballers took Tampa Bay at 07:14 from one place higher in priority. You got the Ravens fallback, which is 3rd of 32 this week — a good outcome from a failed claim, and still a failed claim.

settled.title: Claim Tyler Loop, drop Chris Boswell (15 September)
settled.result: Landed. PFN's Week 2 board has Loop K4 and Boswell K17, which is a wider gap than when the card was written.

settled.title: Start Terry McLaurin in the flex over Bhayshul Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Holding and better supported. Dallas are 19th of 32 and have lost S Malik Hooker and LB DeMarvion Overshown; Denver, where Tuten plays, are 8th. The gap widened from 3.1 projected points to a matchup gap as well.

settled.title: Start Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts (14 September)
settled.result: Reaffirmed on new evidence. Likely ran 22 routes to Theo Johnson's 14 and drew 8 targets, second-most on the Giants. Atlanta are still on Cooper Rush: Tua is day-to-day with an oblique and Penix's ACL return is called too early for this week.

settled.title: Add Brian Thomas Jr. for Stefon Diggs (12 September)
settled.result: Holding. Shoulder resolved to limited practice with Jacksonville expecting him to play. Production still has not arrived — 3 for 40 — and Denver at 8th of 32 is the hardest draw on your roster this week. Review is due after Week 3.

settled.title: Start Jaylen Warren over Bhayshul Tuten (13 September)
settled.result: Held, and weaker than it was. NBC's Week 1 note has Warren taking fewer snaps than Rico Dowdle. What saves it is 5 catches on 6 targets — the passing-down role is the whole thesis and full PPR pays for it. One more week like that and it flips.

settled.title: Drop Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker (13 September)
settled.result: Still wrong and still logged. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4. He is not startable over Warren, but he was never the drop, and that error is why his seat stays closed today.

settled.title: Withdraw the McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith offer (15 September)
settled.result: Retired, and now impossible: Stafford was the drop in this morning's Coker claim and is on the wire. Three sends went unanswered at +3.8 for JuiceJam, which was always the thin half of it.

cannotSee.label: This run fired at 07:40 UTC, forty minutes after waivers processed
cannotSee.body: The schedule calls this the 07:00 Mexico City run, which would be 13:00 UTC. It actually fired at 07:40 UTC — 01:40 in Mexico City. That is why every claim is already settled and the Do-first list is empty. The window to influence this week's waiver run closed before this brief existed. Someone should check what time this task is actually set to.

cannotSee.label: The matchup grades are one board's opinion, not points allowed by position
cannotSee.body: The runbook wants each tile graded on the opponent's season rank in points allowed to that position. Two weeks in, that number does not exist. Every tile here comes from FantasyPros' 15 September Week 2 defense board, which ranks defences as fantasy plays — sacks and turnovers — not as coverage against a specific position. It is the best available proxy and it is a proxy.

I took FantasyPros because every other tile on this roster comes from the same board and mixing them would make the grades incomparable.

cannotSee.body: Every seasonProj figure is identical to the ones quoted on 14 September while weekly projections moved. Carson Wentz, who may start for Minnesota on Sunday, carries a season projection of 0.5 and a weekly projection of 17.0. That field is a preseason artifact and nothing in this brief is priced on it.

cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. You could not see that Footballers had Tampa Bay queued one place above you. Nothing in this file can tell you what anyone has queued for next Wednesday either.

cannotSee.label: Atlanta's quarterback is reported, not announced
cannotSee.body: Bleacher Report's 15 September piece has Cooper Rush likely to start again, sourced to Rapoport on both Tua's oblique and Penix's ACL timeline. Atlanta have named nobody. Kyle Pitts's tile reads Good on the Carolina matchup and that grade is worth very little while this is unresolved.

His tile is graded on the 15 September Sports Illustrated piece instead. Flagging it because a stale page that looks live is the failure mode this section exists for.
